summary.intent: Monitor PR #296 for CodeRabbit review comments and iteratively resolve them until no serious issues remain.
summary.outcome: CodeRabbit posted 19 review threads after a significant wait (136 files to process); all 19 threads were addressed via automated fixes across 8 files.

repo: The repo uses .planning/ and .learning/ directories to provide context to CodeRabbit for PR reviews, enabled by PR #296.
PRs in this repo can be large (136 files), causing CodeRabbit processing delays of 10+ minutes before reviews appear.
Both CodeRabbit and GitHub Copilot are configured as PR review bots; Copilot reviews appear faster than CodeRabbit.

workflow: CodeRabbit requires explicit re-triggering (e.g., a comment) and can take 5-10+ minutes to review large PRs.
Polling for unresolved threads is an effective way to detect when CodeRabbit has finished its review.
The /resolve-pr-reviews workflow (poll → triage → fix → repeat) is viable for automated review resolution loops.

friction: CodeRabbit took an unusually long time to post its review due to the large PR size (136 files), requiring multiple wait-and-retry cycles.
No visibility into CodeRabbit's processing progress — only a timestamp acknowledgment at 13:54 with no ETA.
open_items: Verify that all 19 CodeRabbit threads were fully resolved and no follow-up review comments were generated after the fixes.
The loop was set to continue 'until no relevant/serious comments are being made' — unclear if additional rounds were needed after the 19-thread fix pass.
